scheme_name: Marriage Assistance To Differently Abled Women (Parinayam-II)
description:
The Marriage Assistance to Differently Abled Women scheme, known as Parinayam-II, was launched by the Government of India in the year 2020. 

This scheme aims to provide financial assistance to differently-abled women who are getting married. 

The initiative is part of a broader effort to empower women with disabilities and promote their social inclusion. 

The scheme recognizes the unique challenges faced by differently-abled women in society, particularly in the context of marriage. 

The primary objective of Parinayam-II is to provide a one-time financial assistance of ₹50,000 to eligible differently-abled women. 

This financial support is intended to help cover the costs associated with marriage, such as wedding expenses and other related costs. 

The scheme specifically targets women with disabilities who may face financial barriers when it comes to marriage. 

The assistance provided under this scheme is aimed at improving the quality of life for these women. 

The scheme is also designed to promote the social acceptance of differently-abled individuals in the context of marriage. 

To be eligible for the benefits under Parinayam-II, applicants must meet specific criteria. 

The applicant must be a woman with a disability as defined under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. 

This Act recognizes various disabilities, including blindness, low vision, leprosy-cured, hearing impairment, locomotor disability, and mental illness, among others. 

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years. 

There is no upper age limit specified for applicants. 

Additionally, the applicant must provide proof of marriage or an intention to marry within a specified timeframe. 

Income criteria are also established for eligibility. 

The annual family income of the applicant must not exceed ₹2,00,000. 

This income limit is set to ensure that the assistance reaches those who are in genuine need of financial support. 

The application process for Parinayam-II is straightforward and designed to be accessible. 

Interested applicants must fill out a designated application form, which can be obtained from local government offices or online portals. 

The application form requires the applicant to provide personal details, including name, age, address, and disability details. 

Applicants must also submit proof of their disability, which can include a disability certificate issued by a recognized medical authority. 

In addition to the disability certificate, applicants must provide proof of income, such as an income certificate or payslips. 

Proof of marriage or an intention to marry, such as a marriage certificate or an affidavit, must also be submitted. 

Once the application is completed, it should be submitted to the local welfare department or the designated authority overseeing the scheme. 

The application will then be reviewed by the concerned authorities. 

The timeline for processing applications can vary but is generally expected to be completed within 30 days of submission. 

Disbursement of the financial assistance is typically made directly to the bank account of the eligible applicant. 

The assistance is provided as a one-time payment of ₹50,000. 

This amount is intended to alleviate some of the financial burdens associated with marriage. 

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 

The ministry is responsible for overseeing the welfare of persons with disabilities in India. 

State governments may also have their own departments or agencies that facilitate the implementation of this scheme at the local level. 

For further information or assistance, applicants can contact the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 

The ministry's helpline number is 1800 11 4477. 

Additionally, applicants can visit the official website of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment for more details. 

The scheme is part of a larger framework of initiatives aimed at promoting the rights and welfare of persons with disabilities. 

According to the 2011 Census, there are approximately 2.68 crore persons with disabilities in India. 

Among them, a significant number are women who may face additional challenges due to societal norms and expectations. 

Parinayam-II aims to address these challenges by providing targeted financial support. 

The scheme also aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly Goal 5, which aims to achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls. 

By providing financial assistance to differently-abled women, the scheme seeks to enhance their autonomy and decision-making power. 

The initiative is expected to contribute to reducing the stigma associated with marrying differently-abled individuals. 

It also aims to foster a more inclusive society where differently-abled women can participate fully in family and community life. 

The government has emphasized the importance of such schemes in promoting social justice and equality. 

Parinayam-II is a step towards ensuring that differently-abled women have equal opportunities in life, including the right to marry. 

The scheme is expected to benefit thousands of differently-abled women across the country. 

As of the latest reports, the government has allocated a budget of ₹50 crores for the implementation of this scheme in the financial year 2022-2023. 

This funding is aimed at ensuring that the financial assistance reaches the intended beneficiaries without delays. 

The government is committed to monitoring the implementation of the scheme to ensure transparency and accountability. 

Regular assessments and feedback mechanisms are in place to evaluate the impact of the scheme on the lives of differently-abled women. 

Overall, Parinayam-II represents a significant effort by the Indian government to empower differently-abled women through financial assistance. 

The scheme is a vital component of the broader strategy to promote inclusivity and equality in Indian society. 

By addressing the unique challenges faced by differently-abled women, the government aims to create a more equitable society for all.
